name: What bathroom layout changes are best for older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: What bathroom layout changes work best in older Los Angeles homes with small or awkward bathrooms?
mainEntity.text: What bathroom layout changes work best in older Los Angeles homes with small or awkward bathrooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in Los Angeles often have bathroom layouts that were built for a different standard of living, with tighter footprints, smaller showers, and less storage than modern households expect. The most effective changes usually focus on how the room functions every day: improving the path in and out, making the shower more usable, and reducing visual clutter. In many cases, a smart layout update can transform the room without making it look overly modern or out of place with the rest of the home. These projects are strongest when they respect the house’s existing structure while correcting the worst pain points. The goal is not just a prettier bathroom, but one that fits how the home is actually used now.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often benefit most from better circulation, a more efficient shower, improved storage, and door or fixture changes that make the room feel less crowded. The best layout changes usually solve the original space problem instead of simply adding more finishes.
